title: Exchange Online: change a meeting organiser with PowerShell
summary: The command, transfer limitations and roadmap details are supported by Microsoft's documentation. Licensing should distinguish Exchange Online's published subscription requirement from the absence of a cmdlet-specific licence or meter, and the permissions guidance should be cited directly.

claims.claim: The roadmap status is Launched.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched", "statusKey": "launched"

claims.claim: The release phase is General Availability.
claims.quote: "releasePhase": ["General Availability"]

claims.where: front matter: clouds; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: The record lists Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant), GCC, GCC High and DoD.

claims.quote: "platforms": ["Web"]

claims.quote: "targetDate": "June CY2026"

claims.claim: The record provides no preview date.
claims.quote: "previewDate": null

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; controls[0].governs; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Exchange Online administrators can change the organiser of an existing meeting or meeting series with Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer.
claims.quote: Use the Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer cmdlet to change the organizer of an existing meeting or meeting series.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Autonomy; rationale: impact
claims.claim: The transfer is admin-opt-in: it changes a selected meeting when an administrator runs the command, not automatically on arrival.
claims.quote: This example changes the organizer of the meeting that has the specified EventId value from `chris@contoso.com` to `adele@contoso.com`, effective from the next meeting instance.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; Open questions; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Licensing is unknown because a licence specific to this cmdlet has not been published.
claims.quote: Each user who accesses the Exchange Online service must be assigned to a subscription plan, and each user subscription has its own mailbox.
claims.fix: Set licensing.model to included. Replace the licensing notes with: 'Each user who accesses Exchange Online must be assigned to a subscription plan. No cmdlet-specific licence or meter is documented at the time of writing (November 2026).' Cite the existing Exchange Online service description. Replace 'A licence for this feature is not yet published' in Cost and licensing with 'Exchange Online publishes a user subscription requirement, but no cmdlet-specific licence is documented.' Replace 'licensing is not yet published' in the cost rationale with 'no cmdlet-specific licence or meter is documented'.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The roadmap and cmdlet reference publish no cmdlet-specific licence, price or meter.
claims.quote: Searched: "Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer" license licensing price meter. Read the roadmap, full cmdlet reference and Exchange Online service description; none names a cmdlet-specific licence, price or meter.

claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell supports Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer -Identity <mailbox> -EventId <EventId> -NewOrganizer <SMTP address> to change the organiser.
claims.quote: Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer -Identity chris@contoso.com -EventId AAMkAGRlMGI0 -NewOrganizer adele@contoso.com

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: No admin-centre UI for transferring the organiser is documented at the time of writing.
claims.quote: Searched: change transfer meeting organizer Exchange Online admin center UI tenant switch enable disabled. Read cmdlet reference and search excerpts for Exchange admin center and Exchange Online; no transfer UI found.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Assigned Exchange permissions are required to run the cmdlet.
claims.quote: You need to be assigned permissions before you can run this cmdlet.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; Open questions
claims.claim: The cmdlet reference does not name its required role or role group.
claims.quote: Searched: "Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer" permissions role audit. Read full cmdlet reference, Find the permissions required to run any Exchange cmdlet, and Permissions in Exchange Online excerpts; no named cmdlet-specific role found.

claims.claim: The -Subject parameter can select a meeting by subject instead of -EventId.
claims.quote: Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer -Identity chris@contoso.com -Subject "Weekly Status Sync" -NewOrganizer adele@contoso.com

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: -WhatIf previews the command without making changes.
claims.quote: The WhatIf switch shows what the command does without making any changes.

claims.claim: The roadmap gives continuity and history during role changes, leave or offboarding as uses for transferring a long-running series.
claims.quote: This can be used, for example, to maintain continuity and history of a long-running meeting series in cases where the meeting organizer has a new role, is on leave, or during the offboarding process.

claims.claim: The roadmap says the new organiser can maintain event time, recurrence, attendees and description.
claims.quote: Once the meeting is transferred, the new organizer will be able to maintain all properties of the event including meeting time and recurrence, attendees, and description.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Without a specified transfer date, the change takes effect from the next series instance.
claims.quote: If you don't use this parameter, the series transfer starts from the next instance.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: -TransferSeriesStartDate sets a future effective date for the handover.
claims.quote: The TransferSeriesStartDate parameter specifies the effective date for changing the organizer. Meeting instances before this effective date remain with the original organizer. The value must be a date in the future.

claims.claim: Instances before the effective date remain unchanged in the original organiser's calendar.
claims.quote: Meeting instances before the effective date remain unchanged in the original organizer's calendar.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Instances after the effective date move to the new organiser's calendar.
claims.quote: Meeting instances after the effective date move to the new organizer's calendar, where the new organizer can manage them.

claims.claim: The previous organiser is not retained as an attendee.
claims.quote: The previous organizer isn't included as an attendee on the transferred meeting

claims.claim: The new organiser can manually invite the previous organiser again.
claims.quote: but the new organizer can manually re-invite them.

claims.claim: Attendees in the same Exchange Online organisation do not need to re-RSVP.
claims.quote: Meeting attendees in the same Exchange Online organization don't need to re-RSVP

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Internal attendees' calendar entries are silently updated with the new organiser.
claims.quote: the meeting instances on their calendars are silently updated with the new organizer information.

claims.claim: Internal attendees retain local meeting properties such as Reminder and Category.
claims.quote: Any changes attendees made to local meeting properties, such as Reminder, Category, Show As (Free/Tentative/Busy), and Private, are preserved.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: External attendees and hybrid on-premises mailbox attendees receive an ending message from the old organiser.
claims.quote: Other meeting attendees, including attendees outside the organization or with mailboxes hosted on-premises in a hybrid deployment, receive a meeting message from the old organizer that ends the meeting series

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Those attendees subsequently receive a new series invitation from the new organiser.
claims.quote: followed by an invitation message from the new organizer for the new series.

claims.claim: Attendees outside the Exchange Online organisation need to re-RSVP.
claims.quote: External attendees need to re-RSVP and recreate their changes to local meeting properties.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Transferring a Teams-enabled meeting does not update the associated Teams online meeting's organiser.
claims.quote: For Teams-enabled meetings, changing the meeting organizer doesn't update the organizer of the associated Teams online meeting.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises the new organiser to update the series with new Teams meeting information.
claims.quote: The new organizer should manually update the series with new Teams meeting information so they can join and manage the online meeting.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The new organiser might not have permission to access OneDrive attachments or links.
claims.quote: For OneDrive attachments and links, the new organizer might not have permission to access the file

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft advises removing and re-adding a copy of inaccessible OneDrive attachments or links.
claims.quote: For OneDrive attachments and links, the new organizer might not have permission to access the file, and should manually remove and re-add a copy.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout; Open questions
claims.claim: The roadmap describes user-initiated organiser changes in Modern Calendar in OWA, New Outlook and Teams as a subsequent feature.
claims.quote: A subsequent feature will enable users to to change the organizer via Modern Calendar in OWA, New Outlook, and Teams.

claims.claim: For that subsequent user-initiated transfer, the new organiser must accept before completion.
claims.quote: For user-initiated transfers the new organizer must accept the meeting before the transfer completes.

claims.claim: -Identity identifies the current organiser's mailbox.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the mailbox of the current meeting organizer. You can use any value that uniquely identifies the mailbox.

claims.claim: The new organiser must be a user in the same Exchange Online organisation.
claims.quote: The new organizer must be a user in the same Exchange Online organization.

claims.claim: Additional cancellation and invitation messages are sent for rescheduled instances after the effective date.
claims.quote: More cancellation and invitation messages are sent for each meeting exception (for example, a rescheduled meeting time) after the effective date.

claims.claim: The new organiser might not be able to join or manage the existing online meeting until its information is updated.
claims.quote: If the meeting included online meeting information, the new organizer might not have permission to join or manage the existing online meeting, and should manually update the series with new online meeting information.

claims.claim: After a transfer, the series portion remaining on the original organiser's calendar cannot be transferred again.
claims.quote: After a meeting is transferred, you can't transfer again any portion of the series that remains on the original organizer's calendar.

claims.claim: Only meetings on the user's default calendar can be transferred.
claims.quote: You can transfer only meetings on the user's default calendar.

claims.claim: Meetings in Group or Shared mailboxes cannot be transferred.
claims.quote: You can't transfer meetings in Group or Shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The reference advises adding the new organiser to the mailbox instead for Group or Shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: You can't transfer meetings in Group or Shared mailboxes. Instead, add the new organizer to the mailbox.

claims.claim: The new organiser need not already be a meeting attendee.
claims.quote: The new organizer doesn't need to be an attendee of the meeting.

claims.claim: -EventId must identify the recurring series rather than an individual instance.
claims.quote: The EventId parameter specifies the meeting to change the organizer for. The value must identify the recurring series, not an individual instance.

claims.claim: If the cmdlet is unavailable in an organisation, it reports 'Transfer meeting action is disabled' and makes no changes.
claims.quote: If the cmdlet isn't available in your organization yet, you get a "Transfer meeting action is disabled", and no changes are made.

claims.claim: No tenant-wide on/off switch is documented on the cmdlet reference page.
claims.quote: Searched: change transfer meeting organizer Exchange Online admin center UI tenant switch enable disabled; "Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer" "enable" "default" "organization". Read full cmdlet reference; no tenant-wide switch documented.

claims.claim: -Confirm controls the confirmation prompt for the individual command.
claims.quote: The Confirm switch specifies whether to show or hide the confirmation prompt. How this switch affects the cmdlet depends on whether the cmdlet requires confirmation before proceeding.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference does not state whether a transfer produces an audit record or name its event.
claims.quote: Searched: "Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer" permissions role audit; "Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer" "audit" "logging". Read full cmdlet reference; no audit passage. Search returned general Exchange Server audit documentation, not a transfer event.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls
claims.claim: Microsoft provides guidance for discovering the roles and role groups that permit a particular Exchange cmdlet in the tenant.
claims.quote: This procedure shows the role-based access control (RBAC) management roles and role groups that give you access to a specified cmdlet
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/powershell/exchange/find-exchange-cmdlet-permissions to sources and link 'guidance on finding the permissions required to run any Exchange cmdlet' to that page.

claims.claim: The Exchange Online service description does not mention this cmdlet.
claims.quote: Searched: "Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer" license licensing price meter. Read the full Exchange Online service description and its feature tables; neither Invoke-ChangeMeetingOrganizer nor changing a meeting organiser is listed.

claims.claim: The cmdlet is available only in the cloud-based Exchange Online service.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in the cloud-based service.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: A subject match finding multiple meetings returns a list rather than changing one.
claims.quote: Because the Subject parameter is used, the change happens only if a single meeting matches the subject. If multiple meetings match, the command returns the list of matches so you can rerun the command using the EventId parameter.

claims.claim: Meeting properties, including the description and attendee list, are transferred as-is.
claims.quote: The meeting's properties are transferred to the new organizer's calendar as-is.

controlChecks.governs: Changing the organiser of a meeting or meeting series
